description: Get a company's float on past dates. Two series, chosen with "basis". "daily" (default): one sample per trade date (float shares, shares outstanding, and the source the float came from), recorded going forward since mid-2026 and not backfilled, so early or absent history is expected and an empty rows array is a normal result. Each row carries "source" ("computed", "sec_10k" or a market-data vendor tier) because float quality varies. "filings": a float history rebuilt from SEC filings back to 2023, one point per filing date: shares outstanding minus shares held by affiliates (officers and directors, holders filing Schedule 13D, holders tied to the board (a director at the holder, or a right to name one) whatever schedule they file, and 10%+ holders with no passive Schedule 13G; other passive 13G holders stay in the float). Each point is the float as of its own date, on that date's split basis (not adjusted for later splits). Every point carries "calc" (the subtraction, line by line) and "sources" (the filings it is built from, with verbatim quotes and links). "source" is "ownership_table" (a proxy or 10-K ownership table), "snapshot" (a dated dilution analysis) or "rolled" (a later quarterly share count, minus the last table's holdings adjusted for insider Form 4 trades and Schedule 13D changes). A point with floatLow/floatHigh and no floatShares is a range whose two bounds are the measurement; it has no midpoint value. "flags" state the assumptions behind a point (for example affiliated holders carried at their last table level). A date with no point was not measured, which is not a float of zero or an unchanged float.

basis.description: "daily" (default): recorded daily samples since mid-2026. "filings": points rebuilt from SEC filings since 2023, each with its calculation and cited filings.

days.description: basis "daily" only: lookback window in trade dates. Default 90, clamped to 1-730.

ticker.description: Company identifier: the current ticker (e.g. "AAPL"), a former ticker of a renamed or delisted company (e.g. "MIGI", now BGDE), or a numeric SEC CIK (e.g. "320193" or "0000320193"). A former ticker or a CIK is answered with a `resolvedFrom` block naming the current symbol.

name: get_float_history
title: Get Float History
